quiz.title: Class 12 Integration Ex 7.7 Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the three standard root-of-quadratic integrals and completing the square. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths Exercise 7.7 — integrals of the form root(x²+a²), root(x²−a²) and root(a²−x²)

questions.q: What is the integral of root(a²−x²) with respect to x?
questions.explanation: This is the only form of the three that produces an inverse-sine term. The 'minus x²' inside the root is the signal for sin⁻¹(x/a).

questions.q: Besides (x/2)root(x²+a²), which term appears in the integral of root(x²+a²)?
questions.explanation: For root(x²+a²) the log term is added: +(a²/2)log|x+root(x²+a²)|. The minus sign belongs to the root(x²−a²) case.

questions.q: Completing the square, x²+2x+5 equals which of these?
questions.explanation: Half of 2 is 1, so x²+2x+5 = (x+1)² − 1 + 5 = (x+1)² + 4 = (x+1)² + 2². This is the root(x²+a²) type with a = 2.

questions.q: To integrate root(x²−9), which standard form and value of a apply?
questions.explanation: 9 = 3², so root(x²−9) = root(x²−3²), the root(x²−a²) form with a = 3, not 9.

questions.q: What is the integral of root(x²−a²) with respect to x?
questions.explanation: root(x²−a²) gives a subtracted log term: −(a²/2)log|x+root(x²−a²)|. Only root(a²−x²) uses sin⁻¹.

questions.q: After completing the square, root(x²+4x+8) becomes which standard type?
questions.explanation: x²+4x+8 = (x+2)² + 4 = (x+2)² + 2². Substituting u = x+2 gives root(u²+a²) with a = 2, so a² = 4 but a = 2.

questions.q: The expression 3 − 2x − x², written as a completed square, equals:
questions.explanation: 3 − 2x − x² = −(x²+2x−3) = −((x+1)² − 4) = 4 − (x+1)². This is the root(a²−u²) type with a = 2, u = x+1.

questions.q: What is the integral of root(1−x²) with respect to x?
questions.explanation: Here a = 1, so a²/2 = 1/2. Using the root(a²−x²) formula: (x/2)root(1−x²) + (1/2)sin⁻¹x + C.

faq.q: What does Exercise 7.7 in NCERT Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: It deals with integrating functions that are the square root of a quadratic — the three standard forms root(x²+a²), root(x²−a²) and root(a²−x²). Most questions first need you to complete the square before a standard formula fits.

faq.q: How do I know which of the three formulas to use?
faq.a: Look at the sign inside the root after completing the square. A '+a²' with x² positive points to root(x²+a²); 'x²−a²' points to root(x²−a²); and 'a²−x²' (a constant minus x²) points to root(a²−x²), the only one that gives an inverse-sine term.

faq.q: Why is completing the square needed in this exercise?
faq.a: Expressions like root(x²+4x+8) or root(3−2x−x²) do not match a standard form as written. Completing the square rewrites them as root of a perfect square plus or minus a constant, so a simple substitution turns them into the memorised forms.

faq.q: Which formula produces an inverse-sine term?
faq.a: Only the integral of root(a²−x²), which gives (a²/2)sin⁻¹(x/a). The other two forms, root(x²+a²) and root(x²−a²), each produce a logarithmic term instead.
